newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures slip late, close mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures slip late, close mixed.

text.p: CME lumber slipped from session highs after running into technical resistance on the early shortcovering advance and closed mixed, traders said.
Lumber ended $3.30 higher to $7.00 lower, with July up $2.90 at $374.50 per tbf and September off $0.80 at $365.90.
Early shortcovering and scattered buying were prompted by concern over possible labor problems in Canada as negatiations between woodworker unions and mills continued without result, they said.

Some scale-up resistance was evident on the still-weak undertone to cash lumber. Product movement has been slow. Locals also pushed the spread buy buying July and selling September, pit sources added.
